fixes.explanation: Right, baker. Job says, "…nor is it found in the land of the living." (Job 28:13) You can't just wander around and bump into it. Hang on, because Job has more to say about where it is.

Right on the money, baker. Job says, "Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore." (Job 28:2) So the metals come out of the ground. Getting them takes real digging, like me going to the bottom of the chocolate chip bin.

Busy roads are exactly where this miner is not, baker. Job says he cuts the shaft "Far from human habitation… in places forgotten by the foot of man." (Job 28:4) Forgotten by feet means no traffic at all.

Baked right, baker! Job says, "Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold." (Job 28:6) Two treasures in one spot. That's like finding chocolate chips AND butterscotch bits in the same cookie.

Nice stones, baker, but they're not the ones on Job's list here. He says, "Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold." (Job 28:6) The rocks hold sapphires, and the gold comes in flecks. Keep your eye on the sapphires.

Yes, baker! The miner stops up the streams "…to bring what is hidden to light." (Job 28:11) Hidden things dragged out into the open. I spent years hidden in the back of a junk drawer before I was brought into the light, so this verse hits home.
Not quite, baker. Job says, "No man can know its value…" (Job 28:13) After all that talk of silver and gold, he's talking about worth. The word is value.

Nobody's holding a key in this verse, friend. Job says, "Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor about it.’" (Job 28:22) Abaddon is a name for the place of destruction. Locked away isn't what they describe. A rumor is what they describe.

Guard duty is a noble job, friend, and I take it seriously with my cookie boxes. But Job says, "But God understands its way, and He knows its place." (Job 28:23) Every living thing came up empty, so this turn is about what God knows, not what He protects. Understands is the word.

Yes, baker. Job says, "For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens." (Job 28:24) The ends of the earth and everything under the heavens are in His view. That's why He knows where wisdom is.

Job does say wisdom is hidden, baker, but he never says God hid it there. He says, "For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens." (Job 28:24) The reason God knows is what He sees.

Elders can be a blessing, friend, and I'd trust a few of them with my dough recipe. But God's answer is different. Job says God told man, "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom…" (Job 28:28) Wisdom is the fear of the Lord, not a seat at the elders' table.

Second-guessing myself is my specialty, friend, so I get it. But God says, "…and to turn away from evil is understanding." (Job 28:28) So the statement is true. Wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and understanding is turning away from evil.
